text:
Colorado hosts Pittsburgh tonight, and the model has the home side slightly ahead, projecting COL for 3.40 expected goals to PIT's 3.02. The gap shows up at the defensive end. COL allows 2.44 expected goals per 60 against 3.27 for PIT, while the teams create at a similar rate (3.28 for COL, 3.39 for PIT). At five on five they're close, with PIT at 55% of the expected goals and COL at 56%. On special teams COL has the edge on both sides, with 0.76 power-play expected goals per game against 0.64 for PIT, and a penalty kill that allows 0.34 against PIT's 0.68. COL also draws 4.43 penalties a game, so PIT will want to stay out of the box.

In goal, projected starters Arturs Silovs (PIT) and Mackenzie Blackwood (COL) arrive with opposite pictures. Silovs is at +0.33 goals saved above expected over four games this season after -12.76 across 39 games last year. Blackwood is at -3.19 over five games this season after +8.01 across 39 last year. Neither sample tells us much yet, and the goalies may change.

Form points in different directions. PIT is 1-3-1 over its last five and has taken 47% of the expected goals in those games, winning the chance battle in only two of them. COL is 2-2-1 but has out-chanced every opponent in that stretch, averaging 56%, so its record undersells its play. The model likes Nathan MacKinnon most, with a 45% chance to score and 42% for two or more points, and Martin Necas at 37% to score. For PIT, Sidney Crosby leads at 31% to score, and Evgeni Malkin has the best two-point chance at 22%.
